title: Someone mapped Visa’s tweets and it broke brains
summary:
The quotable takeaway is Visa’s own framing: “lots of people treat twitter like Call of Duty while I treat it like SimCity.” This whole saga is basically the receipts for that—his Twitter isn’t a feed, it’s a city you can wander, with streets made of threads and quote-tweets.

The trigger was May 2020 when Olly Browne (@ollybot_browne) generated a network graph of Visakan Veerasamy’s (@visakanv) hyperlinked tweet corpus. Visa posts the visualization like he just found an MRI of his soul: “every single one of these is a thread,” then escalates to “I’m stunned lol” and “this is fucking art.” The peak moment is when the graph stops being just “cool data viz” and becomes self-diagnosis + method: Visa says he’s basically managed ADHD by using notes/threads to build an “elaborate mind-palace,” and reframes the whole thing as a “cinematic universe, choose your own adventure.” People in the replies treat it like aspirational craft—Qiaochu Yuan (@QiaochuYuan) calls it “goals,” others say it makes them want to “thread more,” and @uberstuber literally asks for “this but in VR.”

Then the conversation mutates from gawking at the graph into tool-building and product dreams. @exgenesis and @nosilverv pitch ThreadHelper as a “serendipity engine” that “irrigate[s] the past,” explicitly arguing Twitter’s attention is biased to NOW and this kind of threading/search is a hack toward a collaborative “Memex.” They imagine a graph UI where you open/fork threads and navigate intersections—“a thread-space-ship”—and even gesture at user-owned data/peer-to-peer infra. The hype eventually cools back into vibes and metaphors (people asking how to “hyperthread” without spamming feeds; Visa later crowdsourcing “favorite threads” to build a master index), and by 2024 it crystallizes into philosophy + longitudinal flex: Visa reposts old threadweb graphs and compares scale (60k tweets in 2020 vs 209k in 2022).

Why care: it’s a window into an alternative use of social media—less doomscroll arena, more personal knowledge graph + relationship-building engine. If you’ve ever wished your posts didn’t instantly fossilize, or wanted a “second brain” that’s multiplayer and actually fun, this thread is the moment people realized: oh, you can *build* the internet you live in.
